findings.description: GIT_ENV spreads process.env when the module loads, before beforeAll sets TMPDIR. So every child spawned through sh()/GIT_ENV gets the shared TMPDIR, not fileTmp, and the guard never sees anything those children make. This contradicts the new comment and the ADR amendment ('its children's included'). The same applies to ci-wait.test.ts lines 28-32. In practice git does not create pup-* dirs in TMPDIR, so no leak is missed today.

Duplicated Code. The `sharedTmp`/`fileTmp` `beforeAll`/`afterAll` guard is pasted into three files, each with an identical TMPDIR save/restore, `mkdtempSync` and `rmSync`. Only the prefix and `fix-round`'s toolchain-cache branch differ. This is the third use, so the "no abstraction until third use" rule now justifies extraction. `src/test/temp-dir.mock.ts` already holds the `tempDir` helper and the decision-100 cleanup, and it is the natural home for something like `guardTmpdir(prefix, { allow? })`. Each file would then reduce to one call. The guard has to stay correct in three places, and any change to the decision-100 behavior (for example the toolchain-cache handling) means editing all three.

The amendment cites "(task t-mvry50b8)", an internal task id a reader of the ADR can't look up. The precedent in `docs/adr/0038-baseline-drift-is-a-new-append-only-baseline.md:21` cites a PR number, `*Amended 2026-10-14 (PR #142):*`. Use `(PR #203)` if you want it to match.
